summary: Six drift type detection with optional automatic active-to-drifted status transition.

context.problem:
Cards make claims about code (codeLinks, boundary, code_patterns), about other cards
(relations, parent), and about the project glossary. Without a single drift query that
classifies divergence into stable categories, fixes are reactive and inconsistent and CI
cannot enforce a regression threshold.

impact.statement: Without classified drift the user does not know which fix to apply.
Without auto-transition the active set silently misrepresents reality.

goals.statement: Detect six drift types - broken_link, boundary_inactive, symbol_changed, heritage_uncovered, pattern_violation, glossary_broken.
Automatically transition active cards to drifted when any drift type is detected, unless --no-auto-transition is passed.
Surface ast-grep pattern errors as patternErrors (not drift) so authoring problems are distinguished from runtime violations.

assumptions.statement: All six drift types listed in project_drift_taxonomy memory are sufficient for the current scope.
assumptions.reevaluate_when: A new drift type is observed in production usage.

flow.given: An active spec whose codeLinks all resolve and whose patterns all hold.
flow.then: No drift is reported and the card stays active.

flow.given: An active spec whose codeLink target was removed.
flow.then: broken_link drift is reported and the card transitions to drifted.

flow.given: An active spec whose ast-grep pattern has invalid syntax.
flow.then: A patternError is reported separately from drift; no auto-transition.

flow.when: drift is detected on multiple cards.
flow.then: Drift is reported but no status transitions occur.

design.overview:
checkDrift composes per-type detectors that read from card-storage and code-binding. The
primary driftType is reported on each card alongside the full driftTypes array. Auto-transition
is gated by the --no-auto-transition flag (always on in CI).

components.name: checkDrift
components.responsibility: Run all six detectors per card, classify primary type, optionally auto-transition.

components.name: per-type-detectors
components.responsibility: Independent detectors for each driftType using code-binding and glossary outputs.

invariants.statement: patternErrors and drift are reported as separate fields and never merged.
--no-auto-transition disables every status mutation while still producing the same drift report.

policy.subject: Every detector
policy.predicate: produce a stable driftType from the documented six.

policy.subject: checkDrift
policy.predicate: not transition status when --no-auto-transition is passed.

policy.subject: ast-grep pattern errors
policy.predicate: be reported as patternErrors not drift.

external.statement: Drift taxonomy and gildash API per type are documented in project memory.

guarantees.subject: DriftType enum
guarantees.breaks_if: An existing drift type is renamed.

limits.statement: Drift detection does not propose fixes; that is the user's responsibility.
Auto-transition is one-way (active to drifted); recovery to active requires explicit set-status.

measure.predicate: A removed codeLink target produces broken_link on the next checkDrift.
measure.method: Integration test mutating source then running checkDrift.

measure.predicate: --no-auto-transition leaves status unchanged on detected drift.
An ast-grep syntax error appears as patternError not drift.
measure.method: Integration test with a malformed pattern.

cons: User cannot tell which kind of fix to apply

alternatives.option: Auto-transition always on with no opt-out.
cons: Breaks CI workflows that need to report without mutating state.

chosen.option: Six classified drift types plus opt-out flag for CI.
chosen.reasoning: Matches the taxonomy decision and lets CI behave non-destructively.
